question_text: Sino-atrial node is called the pacemaker of our heart. Why?

mark_split.label: It makes its own action potential

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: It fires on its own
steps.why: A pacemaker is anything that sets the rate, and the SAN sets it because nothing else has to tell it to fire.
common_mistakes: Writing that a nerve stimulates the SAN. It fires without any outside signal.
Calling the SAN nerve tissue. It is modified heart muscle.
steps.memory_tip: The SAN needs no order from outside, so it sets the pace.
steps.margin_note: The reason comes first. This is a 'why' question.
lines: The sino-atrial node, SAN, can generate

steps.label: It starts the beat
steps.why: Because its signal reaches the rest of the heart first, every beat begins where the SAN is.
common_mistakes: Giving the AVN's position instead. The SAN is in the right upper corner of the right atrium.
Stopping at the definition without saying what it does.
steps.memory_tip: SAN starts it; the rest of the heart follows.
steps.margin_note: Add the position. It is a free extra point.
lines: It initiates every heart beat, so it is

lines.text: It lies in the right upper corner of the RA

insider_note: The marking words are 'without any external stimuli'. Saying only that the SAN is in the right atrium answers where, not why.
